patch.value: A slack posting command can silently lose its preflight webhook gate when the override scope drifts from the declared commands

registerPreflight is scoped to a fixed two-entry commands array (slack notify, slack digest). That array and the commands pm-slack declares via registerCommand are maintained by hand with nothing binding them. If a posting command is added or renamed on one side only, the override silently stops running for it (the runtime matches by exact normalized path) and the command posts with no early webhook validation — silently, because the runtime swallows preflight throws and the authoritative fail-fast only fires once the handler actually runs. A test must bind the scope to the declared commands: every scoped path has to be a command the extension really declares (renames and removals fail the suite), the only declared-but-omitted path has to be the offline slack test preview, and run() has to warn for scoped posting commands without a resolvable webhook while staying silent for --dry-run previews, slack test, and configured webhooks.

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: Manifest-vs-scope audit (the check CodeRabbit asked for on pm-linear #67). Commands pm-slack declares (registerCommand): slack notify, slack test, slack digest. No importers/exporters. Preflight scope after PR #58: slack notify, slack digest. Diff: every scoped path is a declared command; the one omitted command, slack test, is an offline preview (no webhook, no network) and was never gated — the pre-scoping global override's run body already string-matched only slack notify and slack digest and returned early for everything else, so no gate was lost and nothing had to be restored. Remaining defect: nothing binds the scope to the declared command list, which this item fixes with a drift test.

value.note: Extends the scoping test into a drift guard: every scoped preflight path must be a command the extension declares (assertCommandContract), slack test must stay out of the scope, and run() must warn for scoped posting commands without a webhook while staying silent for --dry-run, slack test, and configured webhooks. Test title: preflight override is scoped to pm-slack owned command paths

patch.value: Scope bound to the declared command set in test/smoke.test.ts: every scoped preflight path must be a command the extension really declares (assertCommandContract fails on renames/removals), the offline slack test preview must stay out of the scope, and run() must warn for scoped posting commands without a resolvable webhook while staying silent for --dry-run previews, slack test, and configured webhooks. Manifest-vs-scope audit found no lost gate. Verified: npm test 75/75 pass, release:check exit 0.

value.author: pi-agent
value.text:
Round two, adopting the reviewer findings on PR 60.

Greptile P2 and CodeRabbit Major both said the drift guard checked one direction only: it verified every scoped command was declared, so registering another posting command and omitting it from the scope left the suite green. Both were right, and the fix exposed a second, deeper weakness in my first attempt.

First attempt derived the declared set from real activation registrations and asserted the scope equalled the posting class. That still failed the non-vacuousness probe for the wrong reason: it tripped a hardcoded assertion that exactly three commands are declared, not the partition logic. A hand-maintained literal catching the drift is the very thing the reviewers objected to.

Root cause: isSlackPostingCommand was membership in one list, so everything else was offline BY DEFAULT. The partition was trivially total and could never reject anything. A newly declared command was silently classified as ungated.

Production now names BOTH classes - SLACK_POSTING_COMMANDS and SLACK_OFFLINE_COMMANDS, with isSlackPostingCommand and isSlackOfflineCommand - so neither is the other complement and a declared command in neither is unclassified. The registerPreflight scope and the runtime check inside its run body now both read SLACK_POSTING_COMMANDS; they were two independent string literals holding the same knowledge, which is a second way the same gate could have been lost.

Re-proved non-vacuous: declaring slack broadcast through registerCommand without classifying it fails 1 of 75 with 'every declared command must be classified as posting or offline; unclassified: slack broadcast' - the partition assertion, naming the command. Probe removed, 75 of 75 green, release:check green.
